findings.title: DRY violation: duplicate datetime.now() calls
findings.description: datetime.now() called twice at lines 718 and 723 for same operation.

evidence.code_excerpt:
now = datetime.now() # Line 718
timestamp = now.strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')

# Line 723
now = datetime.now() # Cache for reuse

impact.business_consequence: Minor inefficiency and potential inconsistency between filename and header timestamps.

recommendation.action: Cache datetime.now() once at method start and reuse for both filename and header timestamps.

findings.title: Magic numbers: hardcoded truncation limits
findings.description: Multiple hardcoded values (300, 400) used for content truncation with no semantic meaning.

impact.business_consequence: Difficult to adjust preview lengths consistently. No single source of truth for truncation policy.

recommendation.action: Extract magic numbers to class-level constants with semantic names for easy maintenance and consistency.

impact.business_consequence: If Claude Code directory structure changes, multiple locations must be updated. Increases risk of inconsistency during refactoring.

recommendation.action: Create central path helper function or use existing helpers from core/history_chain.py where appropriate.

findings.title: Complex nested logic: content extraction type dispatch
findings.description: Nested if/elif chain for content types makes modification difficult.

impact.business_consequence: Adding new content types requires modifying central conditional chain, increasing merge conflict risk.

recommendation.action: Monitor for growth. Consider dispatch pattern if more types added. Current scale (4 types) is acceptable.

findings.title: Hardcoded absolute path in dynamic import
findings.description: The _load_history_chain function contains hardcoded absolute path 'P:\\packages/search-research/core/history_chain.py'.

impact.business_consequence: Code fails if package moved or installed via pip. Creates strong coupling to filesystem layout.

recommendation.action: Use relative path resolution based on current file location or proper Python import mechanisms.

findings.title: Complex method: export_chain violates single responsibility
findings.description: The export_chain method handles 7 distinct responsibilities across 127 lines, making it difficult to test and maintain.

evidence.code_excerpt:
def export_chain(self, session_id, output_path, max_sessions) -> Path:
    # 1. Dynamic module loading
    # 2. Session ID resolution
    # 3. Load and validate sessions index
    # 4. Filter and sort sessions
    # 5. Path validation
    # 6. Directory and filename creation
    # 7. Content building and writing

impact.business_consequence: Difficult to unit test individual components. Changes require understanding entire method.

recommendation.action: Extract logical phases into separate private methods for better testability and maintainability.

overall_assessment: The export_chain method exhibits several maintainability concerns including DRY violations, magic numbers, code duplication, and excessive method complexity. While functional with good error handling, issues create technical debt. Critical issues: hardcoded absolute path (QUAL-005) and complex multi-responsibility method (QUAL-006).
